version.description: Worker pool label or alias; defaults to the server's default.

declarations.description: Declarations the code added, with the axioms each depends on.

error.description: Why the check could not complete (timeout, crash, policy, ...).

id.description: The item's id, in batch results.

messages.description: Lean's messages, with positions in the submitted code.

ok.description:
True when the code elaborated without errors and passed every policy
check: only standard axioms, no metaprogramming, allowed options, and
for session checks, the session's original statements.

reasons.description: Why `ok` is false, e.g. "axiom: t uses sorryAx".

tactics.description:
With `detail: ["tactics"]`, one entry each time a tactic in the code
ran, in the order Lean ran them. A tactic run on several goals, as
under `all_goals` or `<;>`, appears once per run, and so does every
alternative `first` tried.

time.description: Seconds Lean spent on the code.

deps.description: Declarations it uses, in its statement and its proof or body.

type_full.description: The type with full names and no notation.

used_by.description: Declarations that use it, most prominent first (at most 50).

Declaration.description: A new declaration and the axioms it depends on.

value_hash.description:
For definitions, a hash of the value, so a proof can't change what a
statement means by redefining something it mentions.

Deleted.description:
`DELETE /snapshots/{entry}`: deletes the entry. Its module goes too once
no entry and no kept module needs it, and then so do the modules it
imports, on the same terms.

removed.description: The modules removed, the entry's own first.

Detail.description: Extra detail a check can return, requested in `detail`.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every non-2xx response.

additive_sibling.description: The `to_additive` counterpart, folded into this hit.

imports.description:
The import header that loads it, when the index's default header
(`import Mathlib` and `import Physlib`) doesn't.

informal.description: A Physlib informal result: stated, not proved.

uses_sorry.description: Depends on `sorry`: not usable as a proof step.

Health.description: `GET /health`: 200, or 503 once the server is stopping.

oneOf.description: Search's state; `null` if the server doesn't search.

status.description: `draining`, with a 503, once the server is stopping.

workers.description: The live workers on the queue; `null` if it can't be read.

score.description: Fused score; only comparable within one query.

snapshot.description:
For a declaration of a snapshot module (named in `module`, with the
header that loads it in `flags.imports`).

summary.description: One or two sentences describing it, when a description exists.

text.description: About 150 tokens for a model's context.

Informal.description: A natural-language description of a declaration.

source.description: Where it came from, e.g. "lsv2-v4.28.0-rc1" or a model name.

LabelsRequest.description:
`PATCH /snapshots/{entry}`: removes the labels `remove` names, then sets
those in `set`. The labels that result must follow the rules of
[`check_labels`](crate::labels::check_labels).

ModuleDecl.description:
A declaration of a snapshot module, with its description once search has
written one (with `PISA_SEARCH_DESCRIBE_MODEL`).

Pos.description:
A position in the submitted code: lines count from 1, and columns from 0
in Unicode code points, not UTF-16 units.

Query.description:
One search. Fill as many fields as you can: each feeds different lanes,
and more fields mean better fusion.

goal.description: A pretty-printed goal state (hypotheses and `⊢ target`).

include_sorried.description: Also return declarations that depend on `sorry`, flagged.

latex.description: The statement in LaTeX, e.g. `S(\rho_{AB}) \le S(\rho_A) + S(\rho_B)`.

name.description: A declaration name, possibly partial or misspelled.

pattern.description: A Lean expression or pattern, e.g. `Matrix.trace ?A = 1`.

q.description: Free text from a person; classified as natural language, LaTeX, Lean or a name.

snapshots.description: Snapshots to search as well as the base libraries (default: none).

verify.description: Check hits against `goal` on a Lean worker (not available yet).

dense_pending.description:
The dense lane was left out because the query is still being
embedded; asking again shortly will likely include it.

verification.description: Set when `verify` was asked for, e.g. "unavailable".

warnings.description: What made this result worse than usual, e.g. a lane that failed.

deprecated_to.description: For a deprecated name, its replacement.

suggestions.description: Closest existing names, best first; empty for an exact match.

error.description: Why the index isn't open yet.

leader.description: This replica leads the snapshot index.

ready.description: The index is open and Qdrant answers, so searches can be served.

env_id.description: Fails with `not_found` unless the server has this environment.

SessionCheckRequest.description:
`POST /sessions/{session}/check`: re-checks completed code from scratch
and confirms it proves the statements the session started from, with the
same imports.

reason.description: Why the re-check failed, e.g. the kernel's error or a timeout.

dirty.description:
See the snapshot API: the module depends on `sorry` or other axioms
outside the allowed list.

entries.description: The query's entries on the module, newest first, at most 10.

verified.description: The module and everything it imports passed the kernel re-check.

created.description: When the entry was created, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

SnapshotList.description:
`GET /snapshots`: the version's entries, newest first, that have every
label the query names as `label=key:value` (split on the first `:`; up to
64 filters), at most `limit` of them (1 to 1000, default 100). Keep
requesting with `next` as `after` while a page has it.

next.description:
Where the next page starts, if this page is full. The page after it
may be empty.

SnapshotRequest.description:
`POST /snapshots`: checks code like `/check` and, if Lean accepts it,
keeps it as a module that later code can import, with a new entry that
holds the module. Code that is already kept gets a new entry on its
module without being built again.

key.description:
Makes the create safe to retry: while an entry made with this key
exists, a create with it on the same code returns that entry as it is,
instead of adding another; on other code it is a `bad_request`. Such a
replay ignores the request's other fields, `labels` and `verify`
included, so it can be `verified: false` with no error after
`verify: true`. Creates that keep nothing don't use the key up, and
deleting the entry frees it. See [`check_key`](crate::labels::check_key)
for the rules.

labels.description:
The new entry's labels; see [`check_labels`](crate::labels::check_labels)
for the rules.

timeout.description:
Lean's time limit in seconds, for building the module including its
imports.

verify.description:
Whether to re-check the code through the kernel. `true` also re-checks
its imports, so the result ends [`verified`](SnapshotResponse::verified)
or has an error, except on a [`key`](Self::key) replay. `false` never
re-checks. By default, only code that uses macros, its own or an
import's, is re-checked.

dirty.description:
Kept although a declaration uses `sorry` or another axiom outside the
allowed list; `result.reasons` says which.

entry.description:
The entry, which the other snapshot endpoints take: the one this create
added, or on a [`key`](SnapshotRequest::key) replay the one the key is
on. It keeps the module until it is deleted. Absent when nothing new
was kept: the code was not kept, or `verify: true` found it kept but
failing the re-check, in which case `snapshot` and `header` are set and
`result` has the error.

header.description:
The header to start code on top of this snapshot with: this code's
imports with its snapshots replaced by the new one. Code with exactly
this header reuses the Lean process the snapshot's builder keeps warm.

result.description:
The check, as for `/check`. It has no `sorries`, and `time` includes
importing the module's imports.

snapshot.description:
The module to import, e.g. `PisaSnap.s1a2b…`, shared by every entry on
the same code. Absent when the code was not kept: Lean reported errors,
or the check could not complete.

verified.description:
This snapshot and everything it imports have passed the kernel
re-check.

version.description: The worker pool version the snapshot belongs to.

SnapshotScope.description:
Which snapshot modules a query searches: `"none"`, `"all"`, or
`{"labels": {"k": "v"}}`, the modules of the entries that have every label.

SnapshotSummary.description:
An entry in a listing: as [`SnapshotInfo`], without the code and the check
result.

created.description: When the entry was created, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

SnapshotVerified.description:
`POST /snapshots/{entry}/verify`: re-checks the entry's module and
everything it imports through the kernel, imports first, skipping what
already passed. A module that fails stops the run and stays usable, marked
as not verified. `verified` and `dirty` belong to the module, so every
entry on it shows the result.

checked.description: The modules this run re-checked and passed, in order.

dirty.description: As in [`SnapshotResponse::dirty`], from the re-check if it got this far.

failure.description: The module that failed, if one did.

StartRequest.description:
`POST /sessions`: runs code containing `sorry`; each `sorry` becomes a
proof state that tactics can be applied to.

code.description: Code with `sorry`s, each of which becomes a state.

pos.description: Where the `sorry` is in the code.

TacticInfo.description: One run of a tactic, with the goals before and after it.

goals_after.description:
The goals left after it ran. A tactic that failed, such as an
alternative `first` dropped, leaves them as they were before.

TacticRequest.description: `POST /states/{state}/tactic`. A failing tactic is a 422 with kind `lean`.

complete.description:
No goals remain for this state's `sorry`. This says nothing about the
rest of the proof; check the assembled proof with the session check.

state.description: The new state. Earlier states stay valid, so a session is a tree.

info.description: Checks Lean code, runs proof sessions, keeps snapshots and searches declarations. Errors are `{error: {kind, message}}`, with a status that follows the kind. `/v1/*` is a 404 on a server without search.
info.title: pisa

post.description: Checks code against the version's Lean and imports. The verdict is `ok`; what Lean, the policy or a limit reported is in-band, in `error`, `messages` and `reasons`.

404.description: `not_found`: an unknown or expired state, session, entry or declaration.

422.description:

limit was hit.

429.description: `capacity`: no worker took the job in time; retry later.

503.description: `unavailable`: e.g. search isn't ready; retry later.
